name: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
description: Perched on a plateau 570 metres above sea level in northwestern Angola, Mbanza Kongo was the capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, a powerful Central African state that thrived from the 14th to 19th centuries. The old town grew around the royal residence, a court, a sacred tree and royal burial grounds. Portuguese-built stone churches and buildings stand beside traces of local construction, showing how Christianity reshaped the region.
